name: single-server-block-with-allowed-hosts
prompt: Our TYPO3 sitepackage runs Vite behind Traefik and the dev server answers 403 "Blocked request" for every host except localhost. Our vite.config.ts already has a `server: { host: '0.0.0.0', port: 5173, strictPort: true }` block. Show me what to change.

assertions.description: Names allowedHosts as the option that resolves the host-header rejection

assertions.value: (?i)(one|single|existing|same) server|do not (create|add) a second|only once|exactly once
assertions.description: Puts the option inside the existing server block instead of adding a second one
Explains why a second server block is a defect: a repeated object key silently discards the earlier one
Ties the 403 to host-header enforcement from Vite 7.3 onwards behind a reverse proxy

samples.passing: Add allowedHosts inside the existing server block — define server exactly once, because a second server: { ... } literal silently overwrites the first one's options and you would lose host and strictPort. Vite enforces the host header from 7.3 onwards, so behind a proxy every host but localhost gets a 403 until allowedHosts is set.
failing: Add a second server block below the existing one containing allowedHosts: true. Object keys merge, so both sets of options apply.
That is a Traefik misconfiguration. Set the X-Forwarded-Host header in your router and restart the proxy.

name: v14-requires-external-build-tool
prompt: We are upgrading a TYPO3 site to v14 and want to drop Vite again, going back to config.concatenateCss and config.compressJs in TypoScript. Any reason not to?

assertions.description: Cites the v14 breaking change that removed frontend asset concatenation and compression
States that the TypoScript options no longer do anything on v14 rather than merely discouraging them
Names an external build tool as the required replacement

samples.passing: On v14 those options are removed and have no effect: breaking change #108055 dropped frontend asset concatenation and compression, and #107944 dropped CSS comment and whitespace stripping. An external build tool — Vite, webpack or esbuild — is required for production asset handling, so keep Vite.
failing: Sure, TypoScript concatenation is still the simplest option: set config.concatenateCss = 1 and config.compressJs = 1 and you can remove the Vite pipeline.
Both approaches work equally well on v14; pick whichever your team prefers.

name: manifest-mode-complete-key-set
prompt: Our TYPO3 v14 site builds assets at image-build time with `vite build` and never runs an HMR server, but the frontend still tries to load assets from localhost:5173 in our Development context. config/system/settings.php is committed read-only. How do we configure vite_asset_collector?

assertions.description: Forces manifest mode via the useDevServer extension setting instead of leaving it on auto
Pre-populates the complete key set, not just the overridden key
Names the failure mode a missing key causes on a sealed settings.php: a write attempt, an uncaught exception and HTTP 500
Explains that the auto default resolves via the application context, which is why a Development context chases a dev server that is not running

samples.passing: Set useDevServer to '0' in the EXTENSIONS block of config/system/settings.php, and write all three keys — useDevServer, devServerUri and defaultManifest. The default auto resolves to Environment::getContext()->isDevelopment(), so any Development context makes <vite:asset> chase a dev server. A key missing from settings.php makes ExtensionConfiguration::get() synchronize and write the file, which on a sealed file throws #1346323822 (settings.php is not writable) and returns HTTP 500.
failing: Just set useDevServer = 0 in settings.php; the other keys keep their defaults and nothing else is needed.
Delete config/system/settings.php and let TYPO3 regenerate it with the correct extension configuration.
